_readme: Skyloft Austin, 507 W 23rd St, as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. Every number cites a key from `sources` in a sibling `_src`; a value with no source says so. Metres, in the footprint's own oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=62.54, W=35.79, +u runs NORTH at bearing 4.5 deg, so u=0 is the SOUTH end and u=62.54 the 23rd Street end; +v runs WEST, so v=0 is the EAST edge and v=35.79 the Nueces edge. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema. Re-massed from a square-on west elevation and an elevated oblique (see scripts/author_skyloft_austin.py).
name: Skyloft Austin

sources.S1: data/snapshots/2026-08-27/buildings.detailed.geojson feature 4c485eb1-3a42-4633-9f67-df5e1c155b5a: name 'Skyloft Austin', num_floors 18, final_height 57.9 (source_height 'overture'), and a THREE-ring polygon - a 62.54 x 35.79 m rectangle with two interior rings of 63 m2 each. Overpass was not reachable from this machine during the pass, so no OSM way id is quoted; the outline is the snapshot's, verbatim.
sources.S2: scripts/bake_westcampus.py, TIER ONE entry 'Skyloft Austin' and its header: '2018, 18 storeys, 442,000 sq ft. The source polygon has TWO 63 m2 holes in it and they are real: the z20 nadir shows two light wells cut clean through the roof plane... Pool on the main roof at the south end (nadir).' Its values: base 6.2 m of BASE_GLASS #454b51, tower #93a3ac, crown 4.0 m of CROWN_COOL #9aa1a6, mech 3.8, deck 'roof', pool (2.0, -22.0, 5.0, 12.0).
sources.S3: Mark Hart Architecture, markhartarch.com/skyloft (the architect's own project page): 18 stories, 442,000 SF, 2018, rooftop pool, furnished apartments, market, study areas, fitness centre, parking, bike parking.
sources.S4: apartments.com / apartmentfinder.com listing for Skyloft Austin, 507 W 23rd St, Austin TX 78705: built 2018, 18 stories, 212 units, '18th-story rooftop pool'. The address is what fixes the building on 23rd St.
sources.S5: markhartarch.com/skyloft photograph 4 of 13 (Leonid Furmansky; saved as mha_04.jpg, 1000x1500): the whole tower in full sun against a blue sky - the near-white panel field with its regular punched-window grid on the long face, a distinctly darker grey panel podium of six storeys under it, a blank end wall carrying scattered narrow slot windows on the same near-white panel, and a glazed amenity volume with a canopy at the top.
sources.S6: mha_02.jpg (1000x1500): the exposed board-marked concrete lift and stair core running the whole height, a full-height glazed stair beside it with a landing at every floor, a mid blue-grey panel plane with scattered slot windows on its other side, the white mass stepping down in terraces to the left, and a dark teal-blue clad cap box with a projecting soffit standing on top of the core.
sources.S7: mha_06.jpg (1500x1000): a near head-on elevation of a long face, shot from the roof of the parking garage east of the building. Ten floors and about sixteen window columns, plus a recessed bay carrying a concrete pier and a glazed stair. THIS IS THE MODULE SOURCE: floor to floor 86 px, window 45 x 55 px, column pitch 92 px, spandrel under the window 30 px.
sources.S8: mha_12.jpg (1000x1500): the Nueces / 23rd corner at blue hour (the NUECES 2300 street sign is in frame). A glazed amenity volume of about four storeys wraps the corner above a dark glazed storefront ground floor; the grey panel podium runs along both street faces; the concrete core with its teal cap stands beyond it; the white mass steps down toward this corner.
sources.S9: mha_00.jpg (1500x1000): the north elevation with the UT Tower behind it to the east - the stepped white mass, the concrete core, the glazed stair, and the grey slot-window panel field, all in one frame.
sources.S10: research/union24th-area/imagery/aerial/skyloft-austin_nadir_z20.jpg (Esri World Imagery, z20, 931x931, 0.1289 m/px at this latitude), RECTIFIED into this (u,v) frame at 10 px/m. Registration: the capture is a few degrees off nadir, so the 57.9 m roof plane sits +10, -62 px from the ground projection of the polygon (= +1.3 m east, +8.0 m north); with that shift applied the two snapshot holes land exactly on the two black light wells, which is the check. Every roof plan number below was read off that rectified plan. Features BELOW the main roof are displaced by (1 - h/57.9) x 8.0 m south in it.
sources.S11: Google Earth 3D, captured 2026-09-05 with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot (imagery 12/3/2023). The useful frame is the one whose own readout says 30 deg 17'12.36"N 97 deg 44'36.66"W, camera 352 m, heading 180, tilt 50 - the building from the north, where the terraced north wing and its recessed terrace bands are directly visible.
sources.S12: data/roads.geojson: Nueces Street and West 23rd Street share the node (-97.74379, 30.28661), 15 m west-north-west of the building's north-west corner. So 23rd St runs along the NORTH edge and Nueces along the WEST edge, and the address 507 W 23rd St (S4) is the north-west corner.
sources.S13: js/westcampus.js SOLID: the West Campus day/golden/night trios for pool, deck paving, turf, mechanical screen and black steel rail.
sources.S14: data/hero_designs.json 'Skyloft' ('Blue glass curtain-wall tower; cool glow at night', confidence 'known'). Recorded because it is WRONG - S5 to S9 show a panel tower with punched windows and no curtain wall above the base - and because no tone here was taken from it.
sources.derived: a number computed from the sources above and marked so; 'unknown' stays unknown.

footprint._src: S1's OUTER ring verbatim. In (u,v) it is (62.54,0) (62.51,35.78) (0,35.79) (0.03,0) - a rectangle, every edge axis-parallel in the frame.
footprint._holes_src: S1's two interior rings verbatim - the two light wells, 63 m2 each. In (u,v): well A u 17.15-27.69 v 14.59-20.68, well B u 39.05-49.58 v 14.60-20.70. `footprint.holes` is NOT read by js/slopes-apartments.js; it is here because it is the measurement, and the blocks below are cut around it. See `todo`.

_frame_src: obbOf(ring) as js/westcampus.js computes it: L=62.54, W=35.79, +u bearing 4.5 deg, confirmed against the console line the generator prints at boot. S12 says which street is on which side.

levels._src: 18 storeys (S2, S3, S4) to 57.90 m (S1). The ground floor is 5.60 m - in S8 it is about 1.85x a residential floor, and S2's own base band for this building is 6.20 m; 5.60 is between them and is what makes the other 17 come out at a residential 3.015 m. Roof slab 56.85 + a 1.05 m parapet = 57.90. The per-floor split is derived; only the total and the count are sourced.
levels._height_src: 57.90 m is S1's final_height, which is Overture's - normally a guess. It is KEPT here, unlike The Standard's, because two independent sources state 18 storeys (S3, S4) and 57.90/18 = 3.22 m per storey, which is a residential floor-to-floor with a tall ground floor in it. No stated height in feet was found: SkyscraperPage and Emporis have no page for this building.

capBlue._src: unused; kept so older readers do not fail

mullion._src: the dark anodised curtain-wall frame of the corner amenity volume (S8): the mullions and the floor-line bands read black against the glass. S8 is blue hour, so the read is taken RELATIVE to a surface measured in daylight in the same frame - the podium panel, #a2a6a8 by day and #7ca0b6 in S8 crop 720,880-780,940, a per-channel ratio of 1.31 / 1.04 / 0.92. The mullion band (crop 470,855-600,868, 10th percentile #1e2e46) carried through that ratio is #273040; entered a step lighter and less blue because a 0.1 m frame at this camera is one pixel wide and reads as its own edge, not as its darkest core.

coping._src: parapet coping: mill-finish aluminium, the same value js/westcampus.js gives The Standard's (STD_CAP). Not separately sampled.

frame._src: site photograph and architect notes: body colour estimated, lighting removed; see author_skyloft_austin.py PARAMS

colours._glass_src: the punched windows' glass: near-black blue-grey by day. S5 crop 560,560-760,860 has the panes at #16415d at the 10th luminance percentile and S7 at #18548f - both under a blue sky, so the day value is entered without that cast; the night value is the unlit pane, and lit panes take APARTMENTS.nightLitTone.
colours._storeGlass_src: the ground-floor storefront: S8 crop 250,1180-700,1260 at blue hour is #383129 to #564e46 with the interior lit warm behind it, which is the night value. LOOK-FIX 1: the day value was that blue-hour read (#3f4c55) and the glazed corner volume came out a black rectangle at midday; a shopfront glass in daylight carries the sky, so it is lifted to #55646d.
colours._loungeGlass_src: the glass of the corner amenity volume. DERIVED, not inverted from a measurement: S8 is the only photograph of it and it is blue hour, and a large reflective plane at blue hour shows the sky, not the surface (S8 crop 470,880-540,925 is #657fab, the sky), so the daylight value cannot be read off it the way the panel's can. It is placed between the two glasses on this building that WERE derived - the punched window (#2a3a45) and the ground-floor storefront (#55646d) - because it is a full-height room glass seen against a lit interior. The night value is the warm downlit lounge S8 shows through it. LOOK-FIX 5: it was entered BELOW the storefront, at #4a5b68, and at the corner the four-storey volume read as one black block over a lighter shopfront - the same defect LOOK-FIX 1 fixed on the storefront itself, in the opposite direction. A room glass four storeys up carries more sky than a shopfront recessed under a soffit, so it is lifted a step ABOVE the storefront.
colours._stairGlass_src: the glazed stair beside the core: paler than a flat window because you see through it to a lit landing at every floor (S6, S9); cool and lit at night. LOOK-FIX 1: at #4a5f6d it read as a dark seam next to the concrete rather than the bright reflective slot S6 and S7 both show, so it is lifted two steps and now sits between the wall and the punched windows.
colours._roof_src: white membrane roof, as it reads in S10; entered cool the way S13 enters top faces.
colours._mech_src: S13 mech (mechanical penthouse screen and condenser units).
colours._terrace_src: the paving on the four terrace decks of the north wing. In S10's rectified plan the three terrace bands are the DARKEST thing on the roof plane - darker than the white membrane roofs either side of them - and S11 shows them as recessed shadowed strips behind a guard. LOOK-FIX 1: they were drawn in `roof`, the white membrane, and from the north the four steps read as bright white shelves flying out of the wall instead of as terraces.

skins._src: one rule per face treatment; every column count comes from a module in metres, never a count.

field._src: square-on west elevation: 8 columns across 29.6 m (3.7 m bay), a row per storey, window 0.78 x 1.40 m

fieldGrey._src: square-on west elevation: 8 columns across 29.6 m (3.7 m bay), a row per storey, window 0.78 x 1.40 m

slots._src: the blank end wall in S5: near-white panel carrying narrow slot windows at about one per 6.5 m of wall per floor. In the photographs the slots are SCATTERED, not aligned; a regular 6.6 m module at the same density is what this generator can express (see `todo`). Slot 0.55 x 1.70 m is read off S5 against the 1.60 m windows two bays away.

slotsGrey._src: the same slot field on the accent panel, which is what S6, S7 and S9 show beside the core.

slotsB._src: the second slot module. The end wall is split into three strips wearing `slotsB`, `slots` and `slotsC`, whose bays (5.2 / 6.6 / 7.4 m) and sills (2.05 / 1.05 / 1.55 m) do not divide into each other, so the slots do not line up into columns - which is how they read in S5.

court._src: square-on west elevation: 8 columns across 29.6 m (3.7 m bay), a row per storey, window 0.78 x 1.40 m

storefront._src: the dark glazed ground floor and the glazed corner volume above it (S8): mullions at about 1.6 m with a transom near three quarters height and a grey fascia under the floor above.

skyLounge._src: the sky lounge in the top of the tower (S5): a band of mullioned glass about two storeys tall, set BACK behind the panel plane with a soffit over it, immediately beside the open roof terrace. Panes read wider than the corner volume's - about 1.5 m against a 1.95 m window two bays away - and the reveal is 0.45 m because in S5 the glass is plainly in shadow under the plane it sits behind. The soffit itself is not drawn (see `open`).

lounge._src: ONE STOREY of the corner amenity volume (S8). Counted at the near corner of S8, where a storey is 240 px: the volume is three panes wide on each face, so the mullion pitch is 1.10 m, and there is a dark band at every floor line with the transom about seven tenths of the way up the glass. It is a per-storey rule because the volume is FOUR of them stacked; see the block's own note.

stair._src: the full-height glazed stair beside the core (S6, S7, S9): one tall pane per storey with the landing showing as a line across it.

concrete._src: the exposed core wall (S6, S8, S9): a blank concrete plane, no openings.

garage._src: the base on the two faces that are not a street - the parking podium (S3 lists parking). S5 shows it behind hoarding and S7 shows only its dark band, so the louvre pitch 0.55 m is a plausible number and is NOT measured: unknown.

slot._src: slim vertical slots in the ribbed metal wall, three loose columns, about every second storey

slotB._src: slim vertical slots in the ribbed metal wall, three loose columns, about every second storey

stripe._src: square-on west elevation: two full-height grey columns one bay wide at u 7.0 and 22.4, windows wider than the field windows, two lights

_signs_src: no sign is modelled: no photograph in S5-S9 and no capture in S11 shows lettering on any face.

roofItems._src: nadir roof plan: raised plant, height derived

square-on west elevation (INFERRED to stand 0.2 m proud of the slab)
site photograph: dark crown box on the core, about 4.6 m above the slab roof; overhang to the north about 2 m (INFERRED depth)

deck._src: the 18th-storey roof pool (S3, S4). S10's rectified plan puts the water at u 1.8-4.0, v 1.8-8.8 in the south-east corner of the main roof, which is where S2's own note puts it ('pool on the main roof at the south end'). Read at 10 px/m off a 0.129 m/px capture: +/- 0.5 m.

items._src: the paved terrace the pool sits in, taken as the roof corner inside the parapet; derived
the green patch north of the water in S10; +/- 0.5 m

LOOK-FIX 3: the guard that encloses the pool terrace. S5 shows a balustrade standing round the open roof terrace beside the sky lounge, and a rooftop pool is enclosed. It stands on the two INNER edges of the paving - the roof's own 1.05 m parapet already closes the south and east sides - so the plan follows the paving read in S10 and only the 1.15 m height is derived.

open: East, south and north faces and the v extent of the stepped blocks are INFERRED from the west elevation.
The two grey pinstripe columns with two-light windows on the slab are not drawn.
The glazed corner bay and the terrace lounges on the steps use the old lounge skin; their depth is inferred.
Heights of the 10- and 9-storey steps are counts from one elevation (+-1 storey).
No SKYLOFT blade sign yet (needs outline lettering).
_balcony_src: no balconies on any face of the photographs
